title: Rising edge batch counter with reset sampling

provenance.adaptation: Independently specified for this project; no public task was copied. The coding assistant chose the state variables, priority order and fixed scan traces, then reviewed the traces against a separate Python transition implementation.
provenance.rationale: A packaging batch counts individual sensor edges and prevents a held sensor during reset from being counted again.
provenance.review: Assistant consistency review of initialization, simultaneous commands, retained state and recovery boundaries; independent Python oracle checked against manual expected traces. Not an industrial safety certification or external expert review.

requirements: Target is valid 1..20. Initialize Count=0 and previous PartPulse FALSE. Error is TRUE exactly when Target is invalid. An invalid Target or Reset clears Count and Complete. Otherwise count only a FALSE-to-TRUE PartPulse transition, then clamp Count to Target. Complete is TRUE when Count reaches Target and remains TRUE until reset or an invalid target; a higher Target can clear it. Every scan, including reset and invalid-target scans, samples PartPulse into its edge memory. A held TRUE pulse after reset therefore cannot cause a phantom count.
scenario: A packaging batch counts individual sensor edges and prevents a held sensor during reset from being counted again.
scan_semantics: At scan k, sample every input once, read retained pre-state q[k], execute one transition, and observe outputs O[k] at the end of that same scan. Updated state becomes q[k+1]. Reset the instance before each test. Step 0 executes normally; initial conditions describe pre-state, not an extra delayed scan. All timing in this task is explicitly counted in invocations, not wall time.
safety_priority: Invalid Target and Reset override counting
Update edge memory on every scan
assumptions: The specification_contract is normative and supplied identically to both frameworks. Output names always denote observed candidate outputs, never precomputed expected values.

atomic_propositions.first: True only on the first invocation after resetting the FB instance.
atomic_propositions.CompleteBehaviorV2: Every observed OUTPUT equals the output of the independent deterministic transition in specification_contract, initialized and advanced exactly as transition_binding specifies.

ltl.explanation: Reset or invalid target clears the batch.
Only rising edges add an item, with saturation.
Edge memory samples the pulse even during reset.
The complete per-invocation relation defined in specification_contract.normative_completion; requires explicit encoding before model checking.

tests.purpose: Held pulses count once and target saturates
Reset while pulse is high suppresses phantom count

specification_contract.observation: I[k] is sampled before execution; O[k] is observed after execution. Initial conditions apply before invocation zero.
specification_contract.normative_completion: 用G(X(qPulse)↔PartPulse)替换P5，并写qPulse初始FALSE；qCount初始0且更新。countAfter=min(qCount+rise,Target)包括Target降低时无新边沿也截断。Complete按当前Target重算，复位/非法优先。
specification_contract.history_binding: Every previous-output name refers to the preceding observed output with the declared initial value. Previous-input memories update on EVERY invocation, including reset, invalid input, stop and mode change. Reference phase/history is independently advanced from sampled inputs by the stated transition rules, never supplied by the candidate.
specification_contract.evaluation_scope: Properties include interpreted data predicates. No claim of export to a model checker or completed formal proof.
specification_contract.transition_binding: Initialize an independent reference state with reference_state_initial. For every sampled input execute the listed deterministic transition once; require EVERY actual OUTPUT to equal its returned value. Do not update this reference state from candidate outputs. This defines the complete scan relation; it is not evidence of ST execution.
